en.title: Before and after agriculture: wealth, inheritance and the institutions of prehistoric inequality
en.deck: Comparative archaeology of prehistoric wealth and power: house-area Gini estimates, Upper Paleolithic graves, Neolithic communities, Bronze Age inherited status and competing accounts of enduring inequality.
keywords: Kohler Smith Bogaard 2017 house size 63 sites
en.regime: Farming expanded storable and inheritable assets but persistent inequality depended on institutions governing succession, exclusion, labor and coercion rather than agriculture alone.
en.key_risk: Mistaking house-area Gini for income, singular elite tombs for entire social classes, kinship for legal inheritance, or cross-regional correlations for a universal causal timeline.

en.search_text: Prehistoric inequality before and after agriculture, inheritance and asset persistence, house-size Gini foragers horticulture farming 0.17 0.27 0.35, Sunghir, Catalhoyuk, Lech valley Bronze Age kinship, egalitarian institutions.

pt-BR.title: Antes e depois da agricultura: riqueza, herança e as instituições da desigualdade pré-histórica
pt-BR.deck: Arqueologia comparada da riqueza e do poder na pré-história: Gini de áreas residenciais, sepultamentos paleolíticos, comunidades neolíticas, posições herdadas na Idade do Bronze e interpretações concorrentes sobre desigualdade duradoura.
pt-BR.regime: A agricultura ampliou ativos armazenáveis e transmissíveis, mas a desigualdade duradoura dependeu das instituições de sucessão, exclusão, trabalho e coerção, não somente do cultivo.
pt-BR.key_risk: Confundir Gini das casas com renda, sepultamentos de elite com classe social inteira, parentesco com herança jurídica ou associação regional com causalidade universal.
watch: Novos conjuntos comparativos de residências arqueológicas
DNA antigo e isótopos sobre posições sociais multigeracionais

pt-BR.search_text: Desigualdade pré-histórica antes e depois da agricultura, herança e persistência patrimonial, Gini da área de casas caçadores horticultores agricultores 0.17 0.27 0.35, Sunghir, Çatalhöyük, vale do Lech, Bronze, instituições igualitárias.

contrary_evidence: Elaborate Sunghir child burials precede agriculture, so social differentiation cannot be dated solely from cultivation.
2024 Çatalhöyük multi-proxy data show temporary inequalities and unequal access to nonstaples without a coherent durable institutional trend.
2017 house-area Gini medians show cross-context association, not causation or world-representative household income distribution.
John Robb 2025 challenges selective elite-tomb narratives and emphasizes collective checks on hierarchy in European prehistory.
Lech valley 2019 microregional genomic study supports enduring multigenerational status but does not establish a single continental origin date.
limitations: House-area Gini 0.17, 0.27 and 0.35 are archaeological sample medians using residential size as proxy, not modern income or wealth metrics.
2017 study covers 63 sites or contemporaneous-site groups and lacks balanced regional coverage of Africa, South Asia, South America and Oceania.
21 populations in the 2009 anthropological comparison are historical/contemporary, not direct archaeological observations of Neolithic people.
Lech valley 104 individuals and approximately 700 years concern a specific microregion and sampled cemeteries.
Sunghir funerary treatment does not establish a tax state or reconstruct all contemporary households.
2024 mound analysis samples approximately 5,000 selected funerary monuments and cannot describe the wealth distribution of the entire living population.
English and Portuguese versions are substantively parallel but require independent QA checking citations, nuance and visual grammar.
Git staging is not publication; independent approval SHA lock and publisher promotion are required.

2017 paper's independent ethnographic cross-check [0.25,0.28,0.44] uses mean group wealth Ginis from unequal category samples n=5,4,8, distinct from archaeological house-size Gini medians [0.17,0.27,0.35]; values cannot be directly paired or differenced.

producer_checks.editorial_novelty: Fifth study in Civilizations, Economics & Power Block A, linking previously published Paleolithic, forager, Neolithic and Çatalhöyük studies to the next Uruk administrative-systems case.
producer_checks.visual_signature: Two matched bilingual charts: archaeological house-area Gini medians [0.17,0.27,0.35] and separately measured ethnographic wealth Gini group-mean averages [0.25,0.28,0.44] (n=5,4,8); a six-row evidence matrix, causal flow, mind map and five-region comparative map. Different observational units explicitly separated.
producer_checks.source_check: Eight identical bibliographic URLs in both locales: AEA, NCBI/PMC, Nature/PMC, PubMed, PLOS ONE, Antiquity DOI, Nature HSSC, Cambridge.
producer_checks.bilingual_parity: 15 numbered analytical chapters plus bibliographies, 8 same bibliographic URLs and source ordinals; two numerical chart series (0.17,0.27,0.35 and 0.25,0.28,0.44) identical in EN/PT, same 3 causal flow chains, one mindmap and 5-region map in each language.
producer_checks.research_depth: English 32,500 characters; Portuguese 35,385 characters; 15 analytical sections and eight academic references; explains the different units and samples of two Gini comparisons.
producer_checks.editorial_status: Producer staged revised bilingual evidence (2 charts per locale) and submitted for independent SHA-locked QA. Not approved or publicly promoted.
